bundle.author: swain
bundle.title: Stop selling, scheduling and suggesting texts after the SMS cutoff
bundle.body:
Finishes Phase 2 and Phase 3 of the SMS compliance cutoff ticket: https://app.clickup.com/t/17tnw2b4zn5. Phase 1 (#2747) closed texting setup 19 days before a candidate's general election and stopped the compliance buildout behind it.

Phase 1 left a gap. A candidate past the cutoff could no longer start texting, but the rest of the product still acted as if they could. Pro pitches, onboarding and the website complete step still sold texting. The campaign plan still scheduled text sends, which also went to Campaign Success Slack and the weekly digest. The Campaign Manager still offered text cards. Each of these sets up the frustration and refund requests the ticket is meant to prevent. They also keep Campaign Success chasing sends that can never go out.

Per the ticket, a closed race now has each text send swapped for a robocall on the same date, so the candidate keeps a voter contact on that day. When a robocall already lands that day, the text send is dropped. The election day text is always dropped, because its reminder robocall lands the day before. The tracker and the plan document read the same swap list from contracts, so the dates and wording a candidate sees always match what Campaign Success sees. Completed rows are never touched. The swap happens when the tracker is read, so the Slack posts and the digest also leave text out for closed races. Otherwise a candidate who never opens the tracker would still show text sends there.

Following Bryan's review, the cutoff is not announced everywhere. Texting claims come out quietly, and the reason appears only where someone would otherwise expect texting: a hover on a disabled text action, or one small notice before they pay for Pro.

For Phase 3, gp-admin's 10DLC widget now shows the texting window, the general election date and the cutoff date. When a candidate says the cutoff is wrong, staff can see why and fix the election date in the campaign form.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes election-relative outreach scheduling and mutates tracker rows on read for closed races; wide UI and agent behavior changes but centered on known SMS cutoff rules rather than auth or payments.
> 
> **Overview**
> **When texting is closed** (19 days before the general election without timely 10DLC filing/payment), the product **stops treating SMS as available** and **replaces planned text sends with robocalls** on the same schedule.
> 
> **Backend:** Adds shared `TEXT_SEND_ROBOCALL_SWAPS` in contracts. gp-api applies swaps when materializing outreach tracker rows and on tracker GET via `alignTrackerTaskDates` (completed/put-off behavior preserved; election-day text dropped). CAS Slack posts, legacy plan Slack, and the weekly digest SQL **omit text tasks** for closed races. Campaign Manager loads `smsCompliance`, **blocks text outreach tools**, and updates prompts/product copy when closed.
> 
> **Admin:** `CvPinStatus` shows texting window status plus election and cutoff dates from compliance state.
> 
> **Webapp:** Surfaces that would launch or sell texting (campaign plan rows, next-task card, manager tasks, race-opponent CTAs, Pro pitches/modals, outreach gate) **disable or remove SMS** and show the cutoff reason on hover where relevant; robocall paths stay open.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 1b2f6b87d6c6d3b5e7a7385da9ba6caa0091ef5c. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

A text-send task the candidate put off acquires `skipReason === 'later'` and a candidate-chosen date. The `dated` map correctly preserves that date (returning `row.date` unchanged for `skipReason === 'later'`), but the smsClosed loop still enters for the row — only `!row.completed` and `flowType === text` are checked — and either swaps it to a robocall or deletes it. This contradicts the AGENTS.md invariant ("from then on the date is the candidate's, so `alignTrackerTaskDates` leaves it alone") and the `skipTask` code comment. `canPutOffTask` returns `true` for all text-send titles (Introduction Text, Persuasion Text, Early Voting Text, Election Day Reminder Text), so the scenario is reachable. No test covers a text task with `skipReason === 'later'` in a closed-SMS campaign. The SMS cutoff CASE block checks only `c.details->>'electionDate'` and falls through to `ELSE false` when that key is absent. The eligible CTE on lines 339-348 does include primary-only campaigns via `COALESCE(electionDate, primaryElectionDate)`, creating the asymmetry: primary-only campaigns are selected as eligible but the cutoff filter is silently skipped for them. The fix is to mirror the GOTV pattern and use `COALESCE(c.details->>'electionDate', c.details->>'primaryElectionDate')` in the CASE WHEN clause. (Falsification: the eligible CTE explicitly uses COALESCE to admit primary-only campaigns, so they can reach the ranked_tasks output; no upstream guard prevents a primary-only campaign with a text task from appearing in the digest.)

                - (NOW() AT TIME ZONE ${EASTERN_TIMEZONE}::text)::date
                < ${SMS_CUTOFF_LEAD_DAYS}
              ELSE false
            END
            AND NOT EXISTS (
              SELECT 1 FROM tcr_compliance tc
              WHERE tc.campaign_id = c.id
                AND (
                  tc.kickoff_sent_at IS NOT NULL
                  OR tc.internal_testing_at IS NOT NULL
                )
            )
          )
